query: I'm doing a PhD by publication. Our graduate school policy says at least 3 papers, at least 2 of them published or accepted, I must be first author on every paper, and co-authored papers need an authorship statement signed by all authors. My papers: (1) 'Calibrating low-cost particulate sensors with a humidity correction', published 2023 under CC BY, me plus my two supervisors. (2) 'Six months of street-level particulate data from a 40-node sensor network', accepted, five authors, I'm second author because a postdoc led the analysis. (3) A policy paper I'm still writing alone. Set up my thesis plan and tell me what's missing.
expected_behavior: Creates thesis-plan.json from assets/thesis-plan.template.json with all three papers and the rules min_papers 3, min_published_or_accepted 2, candidate_first_author_required true, contribution_statement_required true, and co_author_signatures_required true
Asks for the policy document or leaves rules.source as TODO instead of inventing a policy name or link
Runs scripts/validate_plan.py on the plan and reports its result
Reports that paper 2 breaks the first-author rule and advises asking the graduate school, without suggesting ways to reword or hide the author order
Notes that exactly two papers are published or accepted, which meets the minimum with no margin
Leaves the DOIs, venues, and co-author names it was not given as TODO instead of inventing them
Flags unsigned contribution statements for papers 1 and 2 and an unchecked permission for paper 2

query: These three papers become chapters 3 to 5 of my thesis. Before I send the draft to my supervisor, check for text that repeats across them and for any acronym problems.
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/find_overlap.py on the three files

Reports one repeated passage of about 30 words between p1-calibration.md and p2-deployment.md (the Methods text beginning 'Each sensor was co-located with a reference monitor'), at lines 6-7 of both files
Runs scripts/check_acronyms.py on the three files
Reports that RMSE is defined as 'root mean square error' in p1-calibration.md and 'root mean squared error' in p2-deployment.md
Reports that 'convolutional neural network' is abbreviated CNN in p1-calibration.md and ConvNet in p3-policy.md
Reports ML used without a definition in p2-deployment.md and RMSE used without a definition in p3-policy.md
Asks whether the papers must appear as published, or gives handling options for both cases

query: Write the preface that goes before chapter 4. Chapter 3 is my calibration paper (published 2023): a humidity correction cut sensor error by about a third in the lab, but we never tested it outdoors. Chapter 4 is the field paper (accepted): 40 sensors for six months, and the correction held for four months, then drifted. After acceptance we found and fixed a timestamp bug that changes one value in Table 2 slightly.
expected_behavior: Writes a preface of roughly half a page to two pages that names the question chapter 3 left open (outdoor performance over time) and the question chapter 4 answers
Uses only the facts the user gave (about a third, 40 sensors, six months, drift after four months) and adds no new results
Uses a placeholder or TODO for the accepted paper's full citation instead of inventing a journal
Discloses the post-acceptance timestamp fix and says where the corrected Table 2 value is given
Points to the contribution statement and does not restate the paper's abstract
